questions.question: In March 2024, who among the following was elected as the Paralympic Committee of India (PCI) President?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Devendra Jhajharia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Devendra Jhajharia**, a celebrated Indian para-athlete, was elected as the **President of the Paralympic Committee of India (PCI)** in **March 2024**.
 
• He is a two-time **Paralympic gold medalist** in the javelin throw and is regarded as one of India's most successful para-athletes.
 
• His appointment as the PCI President reflects his commitment to promoting and advancing para-sports in India.
 
• The **Paralympic Committee of India** is the apex body responsible for selecting athletes and organizing their participation in international Paralympic events.
 
• Jhajharia’s leadership is expected to bring significant reforms and growth to the para-sports ecosystem in India, leveraging his extensive experience as an athlete.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **About Devendra Jhajharia:**

 
 
• He is the first Indian Paralympian to win **two gold medals** at the Paralympic Games (2004 Athens and 2016 Rio).
 
• Born on **10 June 1981** in Rajasthan, he lost his left hand at the age of eight after coming into contact with a live wire.
 
• His achievements include multiple awards such as the **Padma Bhushan** (2022), **Padma Shri** (2012), and **Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award** (now known as Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award).
 
• He holds the **world record** in the F46 javelin throw category, with a throw of 63.97 meters.
 
 
 
• **Paralympic Committee of India (PCI):**
 
 
• The PCI is the **National Paralympic Committee** for India, affiliated with the International Paralympic Committee (IPC).
 
• Its primary role is to promote para-sports, organize national championships, and facilitate the participation of Indian athletes in international events, including the Paralympic Games.
 
• The PCI plays a crucial role in ensuring inclusivity and equal opportunities for athletes with disabilities.
 
 
 
• **Other Prominent Para-athletes:**
 
 
• **Anil Kumar Prakash:** Known for his contributions to Indian athletics, but not associated with para-sports or PCI leadership.
 
• **Sundar Singh Gurjar:** A javelin thrower who won bronze at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics, but not involved in PCI leadership.
 
• **Mariyappan Thangavelu:** A Paralympic high jumper and gold medalist at Rio 2016, but not the PCI President.
 
 
 
• **India’s Achievements in Paralympics:**
 
 
• India has seen tremendous success in the Paralympics, with athletes excelling in events like javelin throw, high jump, and shooting.
 
• At the **Tokyo 2020 Paralympics**, India won a total of **19 medals**, including 5 gold, 8 silver, and 6 bronze, making it the country's best performance to date.
 
• The success of athletes like Devendra Jhajharia, Mariyappan Thangavelu, and Avani Lekhara has inspired a new generation of para-athletes in India.

questions.question: In November 2024, Hemant Soren took oath as Chief Minister of which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jharkhand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hemant Soren** took oath as the Chief Minister of **Jharkhand** in November 2024.
 
• Hemant Soren belongs to the **Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM)** party, which has played a significant role in state politics.
 
• **Jharkhand** became a separate state on **15 November 2000**, carved out from Bihar, and has a distinct tribal and cultural identity.
 
• Hemant Soren has previously served as the Chief Minister of Jharkhand, making a significant impact in areas like tribal welfare and development.
 
• The state of Jharkhand is known for its rich **mineral resources**, contributing significantly to India's mining industry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About Jharkhand:**

 
 
• **Location:** Jharkhand is located in eastern India, bordered by Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and West Bengal.
 
• **Capital:** Ranchi is the capital of Jharkhand.
 
• **Mineral Wealth:** Jharkhand is rich in minerals like coal, iron ore, copper, mica, bauxite, and uranium.
 
• **Tribal Population:** Jharkhand has a significant tribal population, including communities like Santhals, Oraons, Mundas, and Ho.
 
• **Formation:** It was formed on **15 November 2000**, coinciding with the birth anniversary of tribal leader Birsa Munda.
 
 
 
• **Hemant Soren's Political Leadership:**
 
 
• Hemant Soren is the leader of the **Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM)**, a party primarily focused on tribal rights and development.
 
• Under his leadership, Jharkhand has seen initiatives in education, healthcare, and tribal welfare.
 
• He has emphasized the importance of sustainable development and resource management in the state.
 
 
 
• **Minerals and Economy:**
 
 
• Jharkhand accounts for **40% of India's mineral resources**, making it a vital contributor to the economy.
 
• Industries like mining, steel production, and power generation are prominent in the state.
 
• Key cities include **Jamshedpur** (home to Tata Steel), Bokaro (known for its steel plant), and Dhanbad (coal mining hub).
 
 
 
• **Geographical Features:**
 
 
• The state is characterized by its **forests, hills, and plateaus**, making it rich in biodiversity.
 
• Major rivers like the Damodar, Subarnarekha, and Koel flow through Jharkhand, supporting agriculture and industry.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Birsa Munda:**

 
 
• Birsa Munda was a tribal freedom fighter and folk hero in Jharkhand, who led the **Munda Rebellion** against British colonial rule in the late 19th century.
 
• His legacy is celebrated in Jharkhand, and he is considered a symbol of tribal resistance.
 
 
 
• **Tribal Welfare:**
 
 
• Jharkhand's government has implemented policies to improve the living standards of tribal communities, focusing on education, healthcare, and employment.
 
• Programs like the **Johar Scheme** aim to promote sustainable livelihoods for tribal populations.

questions.question: In June 2025, who took over as the 18th Commander-in-Chief of the Andaman and Nicobar Command?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lt Gen Dinesh Singh Rana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lt Gen Dinesh Singh Rana** assumed office as the **18th Commander-in-Chief of the Andaman and Nicobar Command** in **June 2025**.
 
• The Andaman and Nicobar Command (ANC) is India's only **tri-services command** comprising elements from the Army, Navy, and Air Force.
 
• He succeeded **Lt Gen Ajai Singh**, who was the previous Commander-in-Chief of ANC.
 
• The Andaman and Nicobar Command plays a crucial role in strengthening India’s **maritime security** and ensuring strategic dominance in the Indian Ocean Region.
 
• The appointment highlights the significance of ANC in **national defense** and its role in supporting India’s Act East Policy and maritime partnerships.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Andaman and Nicobar Command (ANC):**

 
 
• The ANC was established in **2001** and is headquartered in **Port Blair**.
 
• It is India's first and only **integrated theater command**, created to ensure better coordination among the three armed forces.
 
• The command is strategically located in the **Indian Ocean Region**, which is critical for India’s maritime security and trade.
 
 
 
• **Lt Gen Dinesh Singh Rana:**
 
 
• Lt Gen Dinesh Singh Rana is a highly experienced officer with significant contributions to India’s defense operations.
 
• He has held various important positions in the Army and is known for his expertise in strategic planning and operational management.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Importance of Andaman and Nicobar Islands:**
 
 
• The islands act as a gateway to the **Malacca Strait**, a crucial sea route in global trade.
 
• They provide India with a strategic edge in monitoring and controlling activities in the Indian Ocean Region.
 
• The islands are essential for implementing India’s **Act East Policy** and fostering maritime partnerships with neighboring countries.
 
 
 
• **Role of ANC in National Security:**
 
 
• The ANC enhances India’s capabilities in tackling threats such as **piracy, smuggling, and terrorism**.
 
• It facilitates joint operations and training exercises among the Army, Navy, and Air Force.
 
• The command is crucial for disaster relief and humanitarian assistance in the region.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Previous Commanders:**

 
 
• **Lt Gen Ajai Singh** served as the Commander-in-Chief of ANC prior to Lt Gen Dinesh Singh Rana.
 
• Other notable leaders include Lt Gen Anil Chauhan, who played significant roles in strengthening India’s strategic capabilities.
 
 
 
• **India’s Maritime Strategy:**
 
 
• India aims to enhance its presence in the Indian Ocean Region through initiatives such as the **Blue Economy** and **SAGAR (Security and Growth for All in the Region)**.
 
• The ANC is pivotal in supporting these maritime strategies and safeguarding India’s economic and security interests.

questions.question: Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) campaign September 2024 was observed from 17th September to 2nd October received participation from over ____ crore people.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1) 30 crore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) campaign** 2024 was conducted from **17th September to 2nd October**, aligning with the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi on 2nd October, which is celebrated as Gandhi Jayanti.
 
• The campaign received an overwhelming participation of over **30 crore people** across India, showcasing the citizens' commitment to cleanliness and sanitation.
 
• The campaign's aim was to strengthen the **Swachh Bharat Mission (SBM)** by focusing on public awareness and active participation in cleanliness drives.
 
• During the SHS campaign, various activities like **shramdaan (voluntary labor)**, cleaning public places, and creating awareness about waste management were undertaken nationwide.
 
• The campaign also emphasized the importance of reducing single-use plastics and encouraged sustainable waste management practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Swachh Bharat Mission (SBM):**

 
 
• The **Swachh Bharat Mission** was launched by the **Government of India** on **2nd October 2014**, with the aim of eliminating open defecation and improving solid waste management.
 
• It is divided into two sub-missions: **SBM (Gramin)** for rural areas and **SBM (Urban)** for urban areas.
 
• The mission seeks to bring behavioral changes in people regarding sanitation practices and create a cleaner and healthier environment.
 
 
 
• **Gandhi Jayanti and Cleanliness:**
 
 
• **2nd October** marks the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi, who strongly advocated for cleanliness and hygiene as an integral part of life.
 
• To honor his vision, the **Swachh Bharat Mission** and campaigns like **Swachhata Hi Seva** are aligned with this day, reinforcing the importance of cleanliness.
 
 
 
• **Participation in SHS Campaign:**
 
 
• The campaign saw the active involvement of citizens, **government departments, schools, colleges, NGOs, and local bodies**.
 
• Activities included cleaning streets, beaches, rivers, and public places, as well as organizing workshops and awareness programs on waste management.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Swachhata Hi Seva Campaign:**
 
 
• It has significantly contributed to spreading awareness about the need for cleanliness and sanitation in both rural and urban areas.
 
• The campaign has played a key role in mobilizing collective action and fostering a sense of responsibility among citizens towards maintaining a clean environment.

questions.question: The Union Budget 2025-26 announced to set up a Centre of Excellence in Artificial Intelligence for education with a total outlay of Rs ____ crores.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Union Budget 2025-26** announced the establishment of a **Centre of Excellence in Artificial Intelligence** with a total outlay of **Rs 500 crores**.
 
• This initiative is aimed at leveraging **Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies** to revolutionize education in India and improve the learning ecosystem.
 
• The proposed Centre of Excellence will focus on **research, development, and application of AI** in areas such as personalized learning, skill development, and teacher training.
 
• The allocation of **Rs 500 crores** underscores the government’s commitment to fostering a technology-driven education system and preparing students for future technological advancements.
 
• This budget allocation aligns with India’s broader focus on **Digital India** and the integration of emerging technologies in various sectors, particularly education.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Artificial Intelligence in Education:**

 
 
• **Artificial Intelligence** is transforming the education sector by enabling **personalized learning experiences** based on individual student needs.
 
• AI-powered tools such as virtual tutors, adaptive learning platforms, and automated assessments ensure **effective teaching and learning outcomes**.
 
• It facilitates **data-driven decision-making** for educators and policymakers to improve curriculum design and teaching methodologies.
 
 
 
• **Digital India Initiative:**
 
 
• The **Digital India program**, launched in **2015**, aims to transform India into a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy.
 
• One of its key objectives is to integrate emerging technologies like **AI, Machine Learning, and Big Data** into various sectors, including education.
 
• Under this initiative, projects like **DIKSHA** (Digital Infrastructure for Knowledge Sharing) provide online educational resources to teachers and students.
 
 
 
• **Government Efforts in AI:**
 
 
• India has established the **National Artificial Intelligence Portal** to promote AI research and innovation.
 
• The government is focusing on implementing AI across sectors, including healthcare, agriculture, and education, to enhance efficiency and productivity.
 
• Initiatives like the **Responsible AI for Youth program** aim to empower students with AI skills.
 
 
 
• **Global AI Trends in Education:**
 
 
• Globally, AI is being used in education to create **intelligent tutoring systems** and provide real-time feedback to students.
 
• Countries like the **United States, China, and South Korea** are investing heavily in AI research to improve education systems.
 
• AI applications such as **Duolingo** and **Coursera** are widely used for skill development and online learning.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of Rs 500 Crores Allocation:**

 
 
• The allocation of **Rs 500 crores** highlights the government’s focus on **enhancing AI infrastructure** for education.
 
• This substantial investment is expected to attract **global collaborations** and partnerships in the field of AI.
 
• The funding will be utilized for **capacity building, research, and development** in AI applications tailored to the Indian education system.

questions.question: By how much the Reserve Bank of India's Financial Inclusion Index has improved from FY 2024 to FY 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2.8%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Financial Inclusion Index (FI-Index)** is released annually by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** to measure the extent of financial inclusion in the country.
 
• The FI-Index is a comprehensive measure that includes parameters like **access, usage, and quality of financial services.**
 
• For the fiscal year **2025**, the Financial Inclusion Index improved by **2.8%** compared to **FY 2024.**
 
• This improvement reflects the success of government schemes, policies, and financial literacy programs aimed at increasing the penetration of financial services.
 
• The index score is calculated on a scale of **0 to 100**, where 0 represents complete financial exclusion and 100 signifies full financial inclusion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **About RBI’s Financial Inclusion Index (FI-Index):**

 
 
• The **FI-Index** was first introduced in **2021** by the Reserve Bank of India.
 
• It is a **single composite index** that provides a snapshot of the level of financial inclusion in the country.
 
• The index is computed annually and is based on three key parameters: **Access (35%), Usage (45%), and Quality (20%).**
 
• The index covers various dimensions such as banking, investments, insurance, postal services, and pension schemes.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the FI-Index:**
 
 
• Helps policymakers identify gaps in financial inclusion and devise targeted policies to address them.
 
• Measures the impact of financial literacy initiatives and government schemes like **Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana** and **Digital India campaigns.**
 
• Encourages financial institutions to expand their services to underbanked and unbanked regions.
 
 
 
• **Key Government Schemes Supporting Financial Inclusion:**
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY):** This scheme aimed to provide every household with access to banking facilities, including savings accounts, credit, insurance, and pension.
 
• **Digital India Initiative:** Promotes digital payment systems and encourages people to adopt cashless transactions.
 
• **MUDRA Yojana:** Provides microfinance and loans to small businesses and entrepreneurs to enhance their financial inclusion.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• The improvement in the Financial Inclusion Index reflects increased penetration of banking services, digital payments, and financial awareness among citizens.
 
• The FI-Index is not a state-wise or region-specific index; it provides an overall measure of financial inclusion at the national level.
 
• It serves as a tool to monitor progress and ensure the equitable distribution of financial services across socio-economic groups.

questions.question: District Hospital Index published by NITI Aayog is based on how many Key Performance Indicators?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **District Hospital Index** is a composite index published by **NITI Aayog**, the policy think tank of the Government of India, to evaluate the performance of district hospitals.
 
• The index is based on **10 Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)**. These KPIs are carefully chosen to assess the overall efficiency, quality, and effectiveness of services provided by district hospitals.
 
• The KPIs include metrics such as **patient satisfaction, staff availability, bed occupancy rates, treatment outcomes, and infrastructure adequacy**.
 
• The evaluation aims to identify gaps in healthcare delivery, enabling evidence-based improvements in health systems across districts.
 
• This initiative aligns with the government’s vision of ensuring a robust and equitable healthcare system, emphasizing transparency and accountability in public health institutions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Key Performance Indicators (KPIs):**

 
 
• The **10 KPIs** used in the District Hospital Index include **OPD/IPD services, availability of diagnostic services, and adherence to clinical protocols**.
 
• These indicators are designed to cover important aspects of service delivery, ranging from **patient care to operational efficiency**.
 
• The data for these KPIs is collected through **health management information systems (HMIS)** and facility-level assessments.
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog:**
 
 
• **NITI Aayog** (National Institution for Transforming India) was established in **2015** to replace the Planning Commission.
 
• It serves as the **policy think tank of the Government of India**, providing strategic insights and fostering cooperative federalism.
 
• Its focus areas include **healthcare, education, agriculture, infrastructure, and innovation**.
 
 
 
• **District Hospitals in India:**
 
 
• District hospitals are the **primary referral centers** for secondary-level healthcare services.
 
• They cater to a large population, often serving as the backbone of the **public healthcare system** in India.
 
• These hospitals provide services such as **specialist care, emergency treatment, and surgical procedures**.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Hospital Performance Evaluation:**
 
 
• Evaluating hospital performance ensures **accountability and efficient use of resources**.
 
• It highlights areas of improvement, enabling stakeholders to address gaps and deliver **better healthcare services**.
 
• Performance evaluation is also crucial for achieving **universal health coverage** and improving **health outcomes**.

questions.question: In March 2025, the 7th meeting of the National Board for Wildlife held at _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gir National Park**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **7th meeting of the National Board for Wildlife (NBWL)** was held at the **Gir National Park**, which is one of the most prominent wildlife sanctuaries in India.
 
• **Gir National Park** is located in the state of **Gujarat** and is famously known as the last abode of the **Asiatic Lions**.
 
• The National Board for Wildlife (NBWL) is a statutory organization under the **Wildlife Protection Act, 1972**, and serves as an apex body for reviewing and approving wildlife-related projects and policies in India.
 
• The board consists of experts, government officials, and stakeholders to ensure the conservation of wildlife and its habitats.
 
• Gir National Park is known for its significant contributions to the **conservation of endangered species** and promoting wildlife tourism in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gir National Park**:

 
 
• **Location:** Situated in **Junagadh district, Gujarat**, Gir National Park is spread over approximately 1,412 sq. km.
 
• **Flora and Fauna:** The park is home to a variety of flora and fauna, including the **Asiatic Lion**, leopards, antelopes, and crocodiles, along with over 400 species of plants.
 
• **Tourism:** Gir attracts numerous tourists every year, contributing to the state’s economy while raising awareness about wildlife conservation.
 
• **Conservation Efforts:** The park has achieved great success in increasing the population of Asiatic Lions through dedicated conservation programs.
 
• The **Asiatic Lion Census 2020** reported approximately **674 lions**, marking a significant increase in their population.
 
 
 
• **National Board for Wildlife (NBWL):**
 
 
• The NBWL is chaired by the **Prime Minister of India** and serves as the apex body for wildlife conservation in the country.
 
• It is tasked with **approving projects** that affect protected areas and ensuring the sustainable development of wildlife habitats.
 
• It also advises the central government on matters related to the protection of wildlife under the **Wildlife Protection Act, 1972**.
 
 
 
• **Other National Parks Mentioned:**
 
 
• **Manas National Park:** Located in Assam, it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site known for its biodiversity, including tigers, elephants, and golden langurs.
 
• **Kanha National Park:** Situated in Madhya Pradesh, it is famous for its tiger reserves and the reintroduction of the barasingha (swamp deer).
 
• **Silent Valley National Park:** Located in Kerala, it is known for its tropical rainforests and is home to the endangered lion-tailed macaque.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Wildlife Protection Act, 1972:** This act provides the framework for the protection of endangered species and the regulation of wildlife sanctuaries and national parks in India.
 
• **Conservation Programs:** Several initiatives, such as **Project Tiger** and **Project Lion**, are dedicated to conserving India’s iconic wildlife species.
 
• **Asiatic Lions:** Unlike African lions, Asiatic lions are smaller and have a distinct fold of skin along their bellies. They are exclusively found in Gir National Park.
 
• **Environmental Significance:** National parks like Gir play a crucial role in maintaining ecological balance and promoting biodiversity in India.

questions.question: Who is the author of the book 'The Shadow Lines'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amitav Ghosh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **'The Shadow Lines'** is a novel authored by **Amitav Ghosh**, a prominent Indian writer, and was first published in **1988**.
 
• The novel is a significant work of Indian English literature and has won the **Sahitya Akademi Award** in 1989, one of India's highest literary honors.
 
• The book explores **themes of nationalism, identity, partition, and memory**, focusing on the interconnected histories of two families across India, Bangladesh, and England.
 
• The narrative is a mix of personal and political histories, showcasing how **historical events** such as the partition of Bengal and communal riots impact individual lives.
 
• **Amitav Ghosh** is known for his deep engagement with historical and cultural themes, and 'The Shadow Lines' is one of his most celebrated works, reflecting his storytelling prowess.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Amitav Ghosh:**

 
 
• **Amitav Ghosh** is an internationally acclaimed Indian author born on **11 July 1956** in Kolkata, India.
 
• He is well-known for his works of historical fiction that blend cultural narratives with colonial and post-colonial themes.
 
• Some of his other notable works include **'The Glass Palace' (2000)**, **'The Hungry Tide' (2004)**, and the **Ibis Trilogy** ('Sea of Poppies', 'River of Smoke', and 'Flood of Fire').
 
• In **2019**, he was honored with the **Jnanpith Award**, India’s highest literary award.
 
 
 
• **About 'The Shadow Lines':**
 
 
• The novel's title, 'The Shadow Lines', refers to the **invisible boundaries**—physical, cultural, and emotional—that shape human lives.
 
• It is structured as a **non-linear narrative**, where past and present events are intertwined, creating a complex tapestry of memories.
 
• The book delves into the repercussions of the **Partition of India (1947)** and the communal riots in **Calcutta (Kolkata) and Dhaka**.
 
• It also critiques the notions of nationalism and identity, portraying their fragility and the subjective nature of history.
 
 
 
• **Other Options:**
 
 
• **Hari Kunzru:** He is an Indian-origin British author known for works like **'The Impressionist' (2002)**, but he is not associated with 'The Shadow Lines'.
 
• **Pankaj Mishra:** A contemporary Indian essayist and novelist, his notable works include **'The Romantics' (1999)**. He has not authored 'The Shadow Lines'.
 
• **Vikram Chandra:** An Indian author famous for his novel **'Sacred Games' (2006)**, which inspired the Netflix series of the same name. He is not the author of 'The Shadow Lines'.
 
 
 
• **Important Themes in 'The Shadow Lines':**

questions.question: In West Bengal, the festival of Durga Puja starts with which of the following events?

__
 
• **Mahalaya** marks the beginning of the Durga Puja festival in **West Bengal**. It is a significant cultural and religious event observed with great enthusiasm.
 
• It occurs seven days before the actual festivities of Durga Puja and is celebrated during the **Amavasya (new moon)** of the Hindu month of Ashwin.
 
• On this day, the ritual of **Chokkhu Daan** is performed, where the eyes of the Durga idol are painted, symbolizing the awakening of the goddess.
 
• Mahalaya is associated with the invocation of **Goddess Durga** and marks the commencement of her journey from Mount Kailash to Earth with her children.
 
• The day is most famous for the early morning recitation of the **Mahishasuramardini Stotra**, which narrates the story of the goddess defeating the demon Mahishasura.

• It is a celebration of the victory of **good over evil**, symbolized by Goddess Durga's triumph over the demon Mahishasura.
 
• Durga Puja involves elaborate rituals, artistic decorations, cultural programs, and community feasts.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Mahalaya:**
 
 
• Mahalaya is considered the day of **Pitru Paksha**, where people pay homage to their ancestors through rituals known as **tarpan**.

• **Other Durga Puja Days:**
 
 
• **Navami:** Celebrated as the ninth day of Durga Puja, it involves special rituals and prayers to Goddess Durga.
 
• **Dashami:** Known as Vijaya Dashami, this marks the end of Durga Puja when idols are immersed in water, symbolizing the departure of the goddess.
 
• **Poila Baishakh:** While not related to Durga Puja, it is the Bengali New Year celebrated in April.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mahalaya's Cultural Impact:**

 
 
• Mahalaya signifies the arrival of Goddess Durga to Earth and is celebrated with immense devotion and enthusiasm.
 
• It is a day of artistic expression, where idol makers finalize the Durga idols by painting the eyes.
 
• People wake up early to listen to spiritual hymns and chants, which set the tone for the upcoming festivities.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement is correct regarding fluid friction?

I. It is also called a drag.

II. It depends on the speed of the object with respect to the fluid.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement I:** Fluid friction is also called a **drag**.

 
 
• This statement is **correct**.
 
• Drag refers to the resistance force experienced by an object when it moves through a fluid (liquid or gas).
 
• This resistance arises because of the viscosity of the fluid and the interaction between the object's surface and the fluid molecules.
 
 
 
• **Statement II:** Fluid friction depends on the **speed** of the object with respect to the fluid.
 
 
• This statement is **correct**.
 
• The drag force increases with the speed of the object moving through the fluid. For instance, at higher speeds, the resistance force becomes significantly greater.
 
• Drag is proportional to the square of the velocity (in most cases) for objects moving through fluids.
 
 
 
• **Additional Factors Affecting Fluid Friction:**
 
 
• The **shape** of the object: Streamlined shapes reduce drag, while irregular shapes increase it.
 
• The **nature of the fluid:** Fluids with higher viscosity cause higher drag.
 
• The **surface area** of the object: Larger surface areas in contact with the fluid result in higher drag.
 
 
 
• **Conclusion:** Both statements I and II are correct as they describe fundamental characteristics of fluid friction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fluid Friction:**

 
 
• It is the resistance force exerted by a fluid (liquid or gas) on an object moving through it.
 
• Examples include air resistance experienced by a car or plane and water resistance faced by a swimmer or boat.
 
 
 
• **Types of Drag:**
 
 
• **Skin Friction Drag:** Caused by the interaction of the fluid with the surface of the object.
 
• **Form Drag:** Results from the shape and size of the object moving through the fluid.
 
• **Wave Drag:** Occurs when an object moves through a fluid, causing waves (common in water).
 
 
 
• **Applications of Fluid Friction:**
 
 
• Designing **vehicles** (cars, airplanes, ships) to minimize drag using streamlined shapes.
 
• Development of **sports equipment** like swimsuits and racing bicycles to reduce resistance.
 
• Environmental considerations in reducing drag to improve fuel efficiency.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• Fluid friction is influenced by factors like speed, viscosity, and surface roughness.
 
• Minimizing drag is crucial in industries like automotive, aerospace, and shipping to enhance performance and reduce energy consumption.

questions.question: The extraction of oil from groundnut is an example of economic activity of which sector of economy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Secondary Sector**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Secondary Sector** of the economy involves processing and manufacturing activities. Extraction of oil from groundnut falls under this category as it involves converting raw groundnuts into edible oil.
 
• The Secondary Sector includes industries such as **manufacturing, construction, and processing**. Groundnut oil extraction is a processing activity, where raw materials are transformed into finished goods.
 
• This activity does not belong to the **Primary Sector**, which focuses on the direct extraction of natural resources (e.g., agriculture, fishing, mining). Groundnut harvesting belongs to the Primary Sector, while oil extraction belongs to the Secondary Sector.
 
• The **Quaternary Sector** involves intellectual activities like research, development, and information technology, which are unrelated to oil extraction processes. Hence, it is not relevant here.
 
• The **Quinary Sector** is related to high-level decision-making roles in government, academia, or business, which again does not apply to the extraction of oil from groundnuts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Primary Sector:**

 
 
• Activities involve the direct extraction of natural resources, such as **farming, fishing, forestry, and mining**.
 
• Examples include growing groundnuts, mining iron ore, or catching fish.
 
• This sector is heavily dependent on natural conditions like soil quality, climate, and water availability.
 
• It plays a foundational role in an economy, often supporting other sectors.
 
 
 
• **Secondary Sector:**
 
 
• Involves the **manufacturing and industrial processing of raw materials** into finished goods.
 
• Examples include the extraction of oil from groundnuts, production of steel from iron ore, and textile manufacturing.
 
• This sector adds value to raw materials and contributes significantly to economic growth and industrialization.
 
• Requires specialized machinery and skilled labor for efficient operation.
 
 
 
• **Quaternary Sector:**
 
 
• Includes services related to **knowledge, information processing, and research**.
 
• Examples include **IT services, data analysis, scientific research, and consultancy**.
 
• Plays a key role in innovation and technological advancement.
 
• This sector typically employs highly educated professionals.
 
 
 
• **Quinary Sector:**
 
 
• Involves high-level decision-making activities such as **government roles, academic leadership, and corporate executives**.
 
• Examples include policymakers, CEOs, and university presidents.
 
• Focused on societal leadership and strategic planning.
 
• Represents the apex of the economic activity hierarchy, contributing to overall governance and development.
 
 
 
• Important Points:
 
 
• The classification of economic sectors helps in understanding the flow of goods and services, employment trends, and economic activities.
 
• While the **Primary Sector** provides raw materials, the **Secondary Sector** processes them to create consumable products.
 
• The **Quaternary and Quinary Sectors** are essential for knowledge and decision-making, driving innovation and governance.

__
 
• The **East-West Corridor** is a part of the **Golden Quadrilateral project** and was initiated by the Government of India to improve connectivity across the country.

questions.question: Why does the human heart has different chambers?

options.text: To pump blood to different organs
To prevent the mixing of oxygen-rich blood with carbon dioxide-rich blood

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To prevent the mixing of oxygen-rich blood with carbon dioxide-rich blood**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The human heart has **four chambers**: two atria (upper chambers) and two ventricles (lower chambers). This structural arrangement is crucial for maintaining the separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood.
 
• The **right atrium and right ventricle** of the heart receive and pump deoxygenated blood to the lungs for oxygenation, while the **left atrium and left ventricle** receive and pump oxygenated blood to the rest of the body.
 
• This separation of chambers ensures the **prevention of mixing** between oxygen-rich (from the lungs) and carbon dioxide-rich blood (from the body tissues), which is essential for efficient oxygen delivery to tissues and organs.
 
• Efficient oxygenation is vital for cellular respiration, which is the process by which cells generate energy. Proper separation of blood types maximizes the efficiency of this process.
 
• In organisms with a four-chambered heart, such as humans, this system supports the higher metabolic rates required by endothermic (warm-blooded) animals. This adaptation is crucial for maintaining a constant body temperature and supporting high energy needs.

• **The Structure of the Heart:**

 
 
• The human heart is a **muscular organ** located slightly left of the center in the chest cavity. It is about the size of a clenched fist and functions as a pump to circulate blood.
 
• The four chambers include the right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium, and left ventricle, separated by **valves and septa**.
 
• The **septum** is a wall of tissue dividing the right and left sides of the heart, preventing the mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood.
 
 
 
• **Function of Heart Chambers:**
 
 
• The **right atrium** receives deoxygenated blood from the body through veins like the superior and inferior vena cava.
 
• The **right ventricle** pumps this deoxygenated blood to the lungs for oxygenation through the pulmonary artery.
 
• The **left atrium** receives oxygenated blood from the lungs via the pulmonary veins.
 
• The **left ventricle** pumps oxygen-rich blood to the entire body through the aorta, the largest artery in the body.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Preventing Blood Mixing:**
 
 
• Mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood would reduce the efficiency of oxygen delivery to body tissues, affecting cellular energy production.
 
• Conditions such as **congenital heart defects** (e.g., septal defects) can cause mixing of blood and lead to reduced oxygen levels in the blood, resulting in fatigue and other health complications.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Organisms:**
 
 
• Organisms like amphibians and reptiles typically have a three-chambered heart, where some mixing of blood occurs. This limits their metabolic rate compared to mammals and birds.
 
• Mammals and birds, with their four-chambered hearts, have higher metabolic rates, supporting complex behaviors and activities.
 
 
 
• **Applications in Medicine:**
 
 
• Understanding the heart's function helps in diagnosing and treating heart conditions like **heart valve diseases**, arrhythmias, and congenital defects.
 
• Medical advances like pacemakers, heart transplants, and artificial valves are based on the detailed understanding of heart structure and function.
